client_need: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
stem: A client with fever, cough, coryza, conjunctivitis, Koplik spots, and a descending maculopapular rash is suspected of having measles. Which infection-control action is appropriate?

options.A: Place the client in an airborne infection isolation room and use airborne precautions.
options.B: Use Standard Precautions only because measles is not transmitted through the air.
options.C: Use Contact Precautions only and keep the client in an open bay.
options.D: Delay isolation until the rash has completely resolved.

rationale: Measles is highly contagious and spreads by the airborne route. CDC recommends airborne precautions and placement in an airborne infection isolation room for a patient with known or suspected measles, with appropriate respiratory protection for healthcare personnel.
educational_objective: Initiate appropriate infection-control precautions for suspected measles.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
source_document_title: Interim Infection Prevention and Control Recommendations for Measles in Healthcare Settings; Clinical Overview of Measles
